title: Galaxy Ampalaya (Galaxy F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Galaxy ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety from East West Seed. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Galaxy ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety, also sold or known as Galaxy F1 or Ampalaya Galaxy F1. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from East West Seed.

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Galaxy ampalaya is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Galaxy F1 or Ampalaya Galaxy F1, this is the same ampalaya. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ampalaya variety finder](/crop-varieties/ampalaya), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 48 to 52 days after transplanting. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ampalaya fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 48 to 52 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** Long and fat, dark green with a glossy skin.
**Where:** Lowland, listed as adapted to Cagayan Valley.
Resistant to downy mildew and cercospora leaf spot.
Flowered earlier than Jade Star, with similar marketable yield, in a 2013 La Union trial.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of eight varieties in the ampalaya guide, an entry in two La Union trials, and named in East West's 2025 story of a Pangasinan grower who prospered with it. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Galaxy ampalaya

Pick by fruit: long and light green for most markets, short and dark for the bitter lovers. Hybrids yield more on a trellis, and some are bred to tolerate the downy mildew of the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Galaxy F1 the same as Galaxy?
items.a: Yes. Galaxy F1 is another name for Galaxy. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Galaxy?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
